traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America, Achlys triphylla (floranorthamerica.org, read 2026-10-17): the leaflets' lower edges are entire and their outer edges cut into a few (usually 3 or 4) coarse lobes; read as coarse outward teeth, so the species does not take Berberidaceae's spiny margin.

generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

generator.params.basal_area.note: The area its `basal` look draws on an organ 1 m long (visual forms leaf blades, 2026-10-15; plantc atlas), so it shades with what it shows: its rosette leaves now take the species' leaf rules and draw its compound leaf, where before they drew the generic simple card (0.235). Since 2026-11-05 its leaflets are wedges, lopsided at the sides and lobed on their square far edges, drawn from its characters: leaf 0.473 to 0.486, basal 0.381 to 0.494.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944), Achlys triphylla, Fig. 1877, p. 219: the single leaf stands 25 cm to 40 cm high, the flowering scape equal to or taller than the leaf (Jepson 1925, p. 395, gives plants about 1 ft).

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a carpet-forming herb: each stalk holds a flat leaf of three broad, fan-shaped leaflets, with a slender spike of tiny white flowers above. Not fitted to measurements. Each stalk bears one leaf of three leaflets (Abrams 1944 p. 219: the single leaf; FNA: leaflets 3), so one leaf at the node, not three trifoliate leaves; the leaf from the node 0.14 m, FNA's petiole to 3 cm and central leaflet to 11 cm (2026-11-05).

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.3 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; white flower spikes.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.inflorescence.note: The Flora of North America's account of the species, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): inflorescences spikes 2.5 to 5 cm long without the peduncle, the flowers without sepals or petals, of 8 to 10 (to 13) stamens 3 to 4 mm long.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its spike drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c): its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants; about 60 flowers, by eye (floras say only that they are numerous), each a tuft of nine white stamens about 5 mm across drawn as a flower of nine thread-like petals. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): no perianth, a tuft of nine stamens (their length by hand: stamens 3 to 4 mm, the Flora of North America, as quoted in search results) round a one-carpelled pistil, from the characters of Berberidaceae and Achlys by the rules at the flowering plants.

traits.leaflets.note: General knowledge of the species, the guides the search returned agreeing: one leaf of three broad, fan-shaped leaflets with wavy, coarsely toothed outer edges (5 to 12 teeth), the blade 5 to 20 cm wide.

traits.leaf_division.note: General knowledge of the species, the guides the search returned agreeing: one leaf of three broad, fan-shaped leaflets with wavy, coarsely toothed outer edges (5 to 12 teeth), the blade 5 to 20 cm wide.

traits.division_pattern.note: General knowledge of the species, the guides the search returned agreeing: one leaf of three broad, fan-shaped leaflets with wavy, coarsely toothed outer edges (5 to 12 teeth), the blade 5 to 20 cm wide.

traits.division_order.note: General knowledge of the species, the guides the search returned agreeing: one leaf of three broad, fan-shaped leaflets with wavy, coarsely toothed outer edges (5 to 12 teeth), the blade 5 to 20 cm wide.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The leaf drawn as a palmately compound leaf of three leaflets (spec rework P4), set from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants: fans (its leaf shape), lopsided side leaflets and lobes on the far edge (2026-11-05). By hand: the stub of stalk the card holds (0.3 of it), side leaflets as long as the middle one (lowest 1) and the side leaflets 115 degrees either side of the middle one (spread 230), leaving open V-shaped gaps between the leaflets, by eye from Jay's photographs (2026-11-05); and one lobe each side of each leaflet's midrib between its corners (lobes 1), its far edge so cut into about five points, Flora of North America's (1-)3-4(-8) lobes. Each leaflet's breadth across its corners, 1.5 times its length, by eye from the same photographs, where each leaflet spans 80 to 100 degrees at its foot: Flora of North America's central leaflet, 4-11 x 4-8 cm, would draw a wedge of under 50 degrees with wide gaps between the leaflets, which the photographs do not show. Before 2026-11-05 a hand-drawn wedge outline 0.95 as broad as long, set 190 degrees apart, left wide gaps between narrow leaflets with fine teeth all along them, which looked nothing like the plant; a first redraw (2026-11-05 21:40Z) closed the fans into a rounded disc, which Jay saw was wrong too.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Achlys triphylla (read on SEINet, 2026-11-05): central leaflet blade 4-11 x 4-8 cm, proximal margins entire, distal margins (1-)3-4(-8)-lobed.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Achlys triphylla (read on SEINet, 2026-11-05): central leaflet blade 4-11 x 4-8 cm, proximal margins entire, distal margins (1-)3-4(-8)-lobed. A leaflet about four fifths as broad as long, a narrow wedge, not a quarter circle.

traits.leaf_apex.note: By eye from Jay's four photographs of the plant (2026-11-05 20:29Z) and Pl@ntNet leaf photographs: each leaflet ends nearly square across its broad far edge (truncate), the edge cut into coarse lobes, not rounded about its foot; the floras read give no apex word.

traits.leaflet_lobe_apex.note: By eye from Jay's four photographs of the plant (2026-11-05 20:29Z) and Pl@ntNet leaf photographs: the lobes on the leaflets' far edges end in points (acute); Flora of North America calls the genus's margins entire to coarsely sinuate.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Achlys (genus, read on SEINet 2026-11-05): leaf blade orbiculate in gross outline; leaflet blades fan-shaped, entire or lobed, lateral leaflet blades strongly asymmetric, margins entire to coarsely sinuate; venation palmate. Achlys triphylla: central leaflet blade 4-11 x 4-8 cm, proximal margins entire, distal margins (1-)3-4(-8)-lobed. Fan-shaped is flabellate.

traits.lateral_leaflets.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Achlys (genus, read on SEINet 2026-11-05): leaf blade orbiculate in gross outline; leaflet blades fan-shaped, entire or lobed, lateral leaflet blades strongly asymmetric, margins entire to coarsely sinuate; venation palmate. Achlys triphylla: central leaflet blade 4-11 x 4-8 cm, proximal margins entire, distal margins (1-)3-4(-8)-lobed.

traits.leaflet_incision.note: Flora of North America vol. 3 (1997), Achlys (genus, read on SEINet 2026-11-05): leaf blade orbiculate in gross outline; leaflet blades fan-shaped, entire or lobed, lateral leaflet blades strongly asymmetric, margins entire to coarsely sinuate; venation palmate. Achlys triphylla: central leaflet blade 4-11 x 4-8 cm, proximal margins entire, distal margins (1-)3-4(-8)-lobed. Coarse lobes on the far edge are lobed, not cleft.
